THE MAIL API CANNOT SET AN ALIAS SENDER: its send request carries displayName and no from field, so an alias must go over SMTP. OVER SMTP HOSTINGER PRESERVES THE CHOSEN SENDER EXACTLY for all six identities (admin@, info@, support@, security@, partnerships@, no-reply@): the visible From, the envelope Return-Path and the DKIM signature (d=provatferi.org, s=hostingermail-a, h=from:...) all carry the chosen address, with no Sender: header and no rewriting, and X-MC-Relay: Neutral on every one. From domain and DKIM domain are identical, so SPF, DKIM and DMARC align for every identity. The authenticated login appears only in X-MailChannels-SenderId / X-AuthUser, never in From or Return-Path. Delivered-To is present on delivered mail, which is what makes envelope-based identity resolution possible. No header is faked anywhere: the provider genuinely supports this.
mail_center_identities_2026_10_26.transport_rule: The mailbox's own address goes through the provider API, which files its own copy in Sent and flags the answered/forwarded source natively; any other identity goes over SMTP. The server decides from the authorised identity, never from the request.
provider_limitations: SMTP leaves no copy in Sent and the Mail API has no append endpoint, so an alias send Bcc's the mailbox to keep a verbatim copy of what went out under an institutional name (mail_center.sending.keep_alias_copy_in_mailbox, on by default; off leaves only the audit record). Those copies arrive in the mailbox like any other delivery.
A message that reached an alias purely through the envelope will not match that alias's filter, because the provider can only search what is in the headers. It still appears under All mail.

cron_timing_note: Cron runs in UTC. One-shot crons scheduled 5-8 minutes ahead on specific minutes, read once via the cron-jobs output operation, then deleted immediately — none left armed (verified empty via a cron-jobs list call after smoke-test-live). One migrate-apply create-cron call in this deploy failed client-side with a transient DNS error (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND developers.hostinger.com) before reaching Hostinger at all; a cron-jobs list call confirmed no job had actually been created, so the retry was safe and did not double-schedule anything — worth that same list-to-confirm check any time a cron-create call itself errors, rather than assuming it's safe (or unsafe) to retry blind. 2026-10-03 addendum: a one-time cron whose minute has already passed never fires and its output stays empty forever (it happened twice, because the gap between reading the clock and creating the cron was many minutes). Schedule >=10-12 minutes ahead, create the cron immediately after reading the clock, and confirm by an ls/file-API probe instead of assuming. A `* * * * *` job running a harmless command is a fast way to read server state; delete it after. `%` in a cron command is eaten by crontab. upload_race_fix_2026_10_05.summary: The stage->switch upload race is fixed. Before: `stage` copied the live uploads tree once (count-checked); uploads the live app accepted until `switch` went to the OLD tree, which the switch renamed to _previous-<ts> carrying nothing over (rows kept, files lost). Now: stage records a hash manifest; switch runs a three-way merge (snapshot / live / staged) until convergence BEFORE the rename, the two renames recover from a stray application directory, and additive post-rename sweeps (immediately, after 10 s, and in smoke-test-live) prove nothing is left only in the retired tree. Collisions are never overwritten (switch refuses before renaming; `keep-both` preserves the other copy under _upload-conflicts/). reconcile <retired> recovers files an older release stranded. See deploy/README.md 'Uploads during a deploy'.

membership_public_cache_2026_10_05.summary: Owner task 2026-10-05: fix Membership Season / public membership page cache invalidation completely. Root cause measured on production BEFORE any change: lib/api/membership.ts fetched the open seasons with next.revalidate 60 s and the types/fees with 300 s, no tags, and nothing told the site about admin changes; the page stayed stale 62.9 s after an admin opened a season and 61.7 s after closing it, and after a quiet period the FIRST request after a change was stale in both languages (stale-while-revalidate) while Laravel already answered correctly. Cloudflare served the HTML and the API as DYNAMIC (no Age; page Cache-Control private, no-store; API no-cache, private) — the only stale layer was Next's server-side data cache.
membership_public_cache_2026_10_05.design: (1) admin changes: observers -> tags -> ONE signed v2 call (nonce, replay guard, allow-list, 1-8 tags; legacy v1 still accepted) sent before the admin's response on the membership screens; the site expires the tags with revalidateTag(tag, {expire: 0}). (2) the clock: both lookups carry meta.valid_until and the site never uses a cached copy past it (it asks Laravel again, uncached) — no cron, no polling. (3) a 15 s safety-net window. (4) Laravel is the only authority at submit: a season is required and must be open at that moment; the form says so when Laravel refuses (data-testid=season-closed), where before it showed nothing at all.
